To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a T‐lympocyte subpopulation (Tar cells) releases a factor that inhibits colony growth of human granulocyte‐macro‐ phage progenitor cells (CFU‐ GM).
a T‐lyphocyte subpopulation, enriched in postthymic precursors, produces a granulocyte‐ macrophage colony‐inhibitng factor.

a T‐lyphocyte subpopulation that inhibites immunoglobulin synthesis (Tar) produces a colony‐inhibitory factor (CIA) that acts directly on CFU‐GM and/or via monocytes/macophages (Mϑ/Ma) and enhances the CIA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of T lymphocytes and their subpopulations as regulators of granulocytic/macrophagic differentiation.
a newly described postthymic T‐cell subpopulation (Tar), a population that inhibits Ig production.

the production of granule‐ and macrophage‐colony‐inhibiting factor (CIA) by a postthymically derived human T‐lymphocytic subpopulation, and the possible role of this factor in the regulation of myelopoiesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data support the hypothesis that a T‐lymphotropic, postthymic, precursor cell, capable of inhibiting Ig synthesis (Tar), is also capable of producing a colony‐inhibitory activity (CIA), which is not interferon.
PHA‐stimulated Tar cells secrete a factor which is capable of inhibiting the growth of CFU‐GM.
the Tar subpopulation, which has been shown to be capable of inhibiting Ig synthesis, is also capable of inhibiting granulopoiesis and macrophage differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PHA‐activated T‐cells release a factor that stimulates colony‐forming units‐granulocyte/macrophages (CFU GM), and that a subpopulation of PHA‐activated Tar cells release a granulocyte‐colony inhibiting factor (CIF).
the Tar cell‐derived inhibitory activity is not an interferon, but is produced in a PHA‐stimulated T‐cell subpopulation and is capable of inhibiting the growth of granulocyte macrophage colonies.
a T‐lympocyte subpopulation that inhibts Ig synthesis, the Tar subpopulation, also releases a factor that inhibits CFU‐GM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Tar cells, a post‐thymic precursor population that can be isolated from human peripheral blood, release a factor that inhibits CFU‐GM colony growth in vitro.
the Tar cells, a post thymic precursor T cell subpopulation, can produce a factor that inhibits granulocyte and monocyte/macrophage colony formation.

a T‐cell subpopulation, which has the ability to inhibit Ig synthesis and to suppress autologous rosetting (Tar cells), also has the ability to release a factor that inhibits CFU‐GM colony growth in vitro.
